name: Beor
title: Father of the prophet Balaam
summary: Beor is primarily known as the father of Balaam, the pagan prophet who was hired by Balak, king of Moab, to curse Israel. Although little is known about Beor personally, his name is linked to one of the most well-known prophetic stories in the Old Testament. He is mentioned repeatedly in the Bible as an identifier for his son Balaam.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as Balaam's father in Numbers
keyEvents.description: Beor is identified as the father of Balaam when Balak, king of Moab, sends for Balaam to curse the people of Israel.

keyEvents.title: Balaam's mission from Balak
keyEvents.description: Balaam, son of Beor, is repeatedly mentioned in connection with Balak's attempts to get him to curse Israel, but God turns the curse into a blessing.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Deuteronomy
keyEvents.description: Moses reminds the people of Israel about the incident with Balaam, son of Beor, and how the Lord refused to listen to Balaam and turned the curse into a blessing.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Joshua
keyEvents.description: Balaam, son of Beor, is mentioned in connection with the Israelites killing him with the sword during the conquest of the land.

keyEvents.title: Warnings in the New Testament
keyEvents.description: Balaam son of Beor is mentioned in 2 Peter as a warning example of one who loved unjust gain and left the right path.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the Book of Micah
keyEvents.description: The prophet Micah reminds the people of Balak's plans and Balaam son of Beor's response, so that they may know the Lord's righteous deeds.
